title: Size loss in 65,660 TESS flare trials leaves a CPV host flare excess under shared size and width laws
abstract: We test whether measured flare-size loss explains the excess flare rate of complex periodic variable (CPV) hosts. We use 65,660 released artificial flare trials in 3,283 TESS sectors. Detected trials with input equivalent duration of 100–300 s recover median sizes of 0.807 of input in hosts and 0.825 in comparison stars. We calculate the probability that each trial both is detected and passes a measured size cut. With a shared differential size exponent of 1.8 and log-uniform widths of 2–30 minutes, the adjusted host-to-comparison rate ratio at a 100 s cut is 1.686. A joint star bootstrap gives a 95% interval of 1.478–1.903. The same stars and covariates with the published detection-only correction give 1.664. Direct response variants give ratios of 1.658–1.726. Size loss changes the rate normalization in both groups but does not remove their relative excess. The result strengthens this association against one measurement error. It does not establish a distinct energy distribution or a source of occulting material. Prescribed flare shapes, shared size laws, untested tails and reused labels limit the inference. Code, aggregate evidence and exact input hashes are included; external record tables stay outside the bundle.

Middle: direct-response flare rate ratios under common size-law exponents, with conditional star-cluster 95% limits. Right: original detection-only offsets and size-migration offsets on the same sample. The primary 100 s joint bootstrap interval is 1.478–1.903.

citations.reason: Reuses released flare trials and counts. Finds size loss but shows that a direct size-threshold response preserves the adjusted relative flare excess under specified laws.
Reads TIC and Gaia BP-RP as scratch-only regression covariates.
